task.description: Idiom/scope gate on REQ-228 (entity event registration + create/update/delete record commands, Letflow.EventStore.append_multi/3 refactor, entity_record_latest/entity_type_instances tables) per WF-02 Step 2d -- independently re-verify compile/format/test, design fidelity, AC coverage, the 4 flagged ELIXIR-DEV discrepancies, scope discipline, OTP idiom, migration idiom, and test-infra side-effects, trusting nothing in prior handoffs.

result.note:
Own runs, own output (all quoted numbers are from commands this REVIEWER ran itself, not copied from prior handoffs): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean, `mix format --check-formatted` clean. `mix test test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs` -> 21/21 passed. Regression: `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` -> 150/150 passed; `mix test test/letflow/entities/` -> 84/84 passed; `mix test test/letflow/engine/` -> 977 passed (1 property, 976 tests), 16 excluded, 0 failures. Figures match ELIXIR-DEV's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's own numbers, independently reproduced rather than trusted. Test-infra side-effect verified from a clean slate as instructed: ran `MIX_ENV=test mix run -e 'Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query!(Letflow.Repo, "DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS tenant_template CASCADE", [])'`, then `mix test test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs` forced a fresh tenant_template rebuild from the full migration manifest (including the two new REQ-228 migrations) -- 21/21 passed, no TENANT_TEMPLATE_SELF_CHECK_FAILED.

Design fidelity: module names/paths/signatures match §3 exactly (Letflow.Entities.Records, Letflow.Entities.EventTypes, Letflow.Entities.EntityTypeInstance, Letflow.Entities.Record.Latest). Migration column/index shapes read directly against §6.1/§6.2: entity_record_latest carries id/entity_type/record_id/field_values/deleted/entity_def_version/last_event_global_seq + timestamps with unique_index(entity_type, record_id) exactly as specified; entity_type_instances carries entity_type (PK)/instance_id/inserted_at exactly as specified (the one intentional index deviation is discrepancy #4 below). append_multi/3's signature, step composition, and error-tuple passthrough match §3.1/§3.3 verbatim -- read lib/letflow/event_store.ex's diff directly: build_multi_composable/2 is a single extracted body that build_multi/1 (append/2's own path) and append_multi/3 (new) both call; not a copy-pasted near-duplicate. append/2 and append_platform_event/2 are byte-identical to before (only the private build_multi/1 body moved).

All 8 ACs have genuine, specific tests -- read test/letflow/entities/records_test.exs directly and cite: AC1 (event-type registration) -> lines 134-163 (describe "AC1"). AC2 (atomicity + forced-failure rollback) -> lines 171-229 (describe "AC2", the second test injects a failing Multi.run/3 step in place of :upsert_record_latest and asserts both Event and Latest counts are 0 afterward). AC3 (idempotent replay returns ORIGINAL record) -> lines 236-272 (describe "AC3", including a third-submission test). AC4 (REQ-227 rejection, zero events) -> lines 279-310. AC5 (one synthetic instance row per TYPE across 3 records) -> lines 317-342. AC6 (design states + justifies the per-type decision) -> satisfied by design.md §2 itself, cross-referenced by the AC5/AC6 test's own comment at line 337. AC7 (outer envelope vs. inner validation each independently exercised, moduledoc states which validates which) -> lines 373-411 (two tests, one bypassing the command function to hit Registry.validate_payload/3 directly with a malformed envelope, one hitting only the inner enum check) plus Letflow.Entities.EventTypes's moduledoc (event_types.ex lines 10-18) and Letflow.Entities.Records's moduledoc (records.ex lines 13-23) both stating the split explicitly. AC8 (mix test/compile pass) -> this handoff's own commands above; scope check (no route/controller) -> lines 577-587, independently re-confirmed via git diff --stat (below).

The 4 flagged discrepancies, assessed for idiom/design-fidelity/correctness (not security -- SECURITY-REVIEWER already covered that ground and PASSed):

(a) entity_type_instance_guard as an eager pre-Multi call instead of a lazy Multi.run/3 step: the RIGHT call, not merely a safe one. The design's own §3.1 literal signature (`append_multi(multi, attrs, opts)`) requires attrs[:instance_id] to be a concrete value at the call site, which is plain Elixir code executed before any Multi.run/3 step's `changes` map exists -- the design's own §3.2 framing was internally inconsistent with its own §3.1 signature, a genuine design-doc gap, not implementation laziness. get_or_create/2's insert-then-on_conflict::nothing-then-re-select protocol is exactly the same race-safe idiom this codebase's own assign_sequence/3 and claim_idempotency/3 already use (verified by reading event_store.ex's own M2/M3 implementations) -- no correctness or idiom regression, and reusing an established idiom instead of inventing a new one is the more idiomatic choice available.

(b) entity_def_version's string (hex) vs. the design's literal "integer" envelope type: the RIGHT call. logical_shape_version is a :binary content-hash column (confirmed against Letflow.Entities.EntityDefinition's own schema) -- the design's own §4.1 table asserting "integer" while simultaneously naming this exact field's role was self-contradictory; JSON cannot carry a raw binary hash as a bare integer or unencoded string. Base16 (hex) encode/decode is a fixed-alphabet, fully self-validating, fail-closed round-trip (Base.decode16! raises on malformed input rather than silently coercing) -- correctly implemented and correctly documented as resolving the design's own explicitly-flagged open question (§8 item 1), not a silent divergence.

(c) definition_document/1's atom-keyed conversion helper: a genuine, narrowly-scoped gap-fill, not scope creep or an abstraction reached for too early. Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 returns a string-keyed jsonb-decoded map; Record.Validator.build_record_schema/1 (REQ-227) expects Definition.t()'s atom-keyed shape verbatim -- a real interface mismatch between two already-merged modules (REQ-226 and REQ-227) that neither of those requirements' own test suites happened to exercise together. String.to_existing_atom/1 (not String.to_atom/1) is the correct fail-closed choice against the codebase's own already-compiled closed field-type atom set -- a malformed/unexpected "type" string raises rather than producing a silently-wrong atom key. This is worth noting as a signal that REQ-226/REQ-227's integration boundary wasn't validated end-to-end before REQ-228 needed it, but the fix itself is a small, local, single-purpose function, not new machinery -- does not block PASS, and is not the kind of representable-invalid-state gap that calls for a docs/issues/ type-safety filing (the atom set is closed and compiled-in; the conversion is a data-shape bridge, not a new modeling gap).

(d) removed redundant unique_index on entity_type_instances.entity_type: the RIGHT call. entity_type is the table's own primary key (confirmed in the migration, line 25) -- a second named unique index over the identical single column adds zero additional guarantee and, empirically, broke the shared tenant-template clone tooling (42P07 duplicate_table). Removing it and pointing insert_changeset/2's unique_constraint/3 at the PK's own default index name (entity_type_instances_pkey) is correct Ecto/Postgres idiom, not a design shortcut -- AC5's uniqueness guarantee is unaffected since the PK alone already enforces it. Migration file's own comment explains this clearly for a future reader.

All four deviations are well-reasoned engineering calls that correct genuine gaps/errors in the design artefact itself, each documented in the relevant module's own moduledoc or migration comment (this project's "flag, don't silently diverge" convention followed correctly) -- none of the four indicates the design should have been sent back for rework; each is the kind of concrete-implementation-detail resolution a design artefact is expected to leave to ELIXIR-DEV when explicitly flagged as an open question (as 3 of the 4 were, verbatim, in design.md §8).

Scope discipline: `git diff ec8766d2..HEAD --stat` -- 19 files changed (7 handoff JSONs, 1 design doc, 5 new lib/letflow/entities/* + event_store.ex modification + tenant_provisioning.ex's 6-line migration-manifest registration, 2 new migrations, 3 test files). No route/controller/web files. No REQ-229 (projection/replay/rebuild) logic beyond the single entity_record_latest write inside each command's own transaction, exactly as design §5.3/§1 scope this out.

IDIOM/OTP: no GenServer/gen_statem/process introduced -- plain Ecto.Multi + Ecto.Repo throughout, correctly matching REQ-045's process-vs-row decision and the REQ-226/227 precedent. append_multi/3's extraction (build_multi_composable/2) is a clean, single-source-of-truth refactor, confirmed by reading the actual diff -- not a duplicated near-copy that will drift; append/2's own behavior is provably unchanged (150/150 event_store tests, 977 engine tests including TaskActivation.append_multi/6's own usage, all passing).

Migration idiom: both new migrations match REQ-226's 20260906000001_create_entity_definitions.exs precedent -- identical `if prefix() do ... end` guard block, explicit binary_id primary key style (entity_record_latest) or intentional single-column string PK (entity_type_instances, justified in-file), named indexes, `timestamps()` convention (entity_type_instances correctly omits updated_at, matching its stated immutable-once-created design). Both correctly registered in TenantProvisioning's migration manifest (tenant_provisioning.ex diff, 6 lines).

Test infra: test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_test.exs's 39->41 bump is correct (two new tables, entity_record_latest and entity_type_instances, both added to the expected-tables list) and verified end-to-end via the forced tenant_template rebuild above -- no self-check failure.

Type-safety scan (per this gate's own item 3, non-blocking): no new class of invalid state introduced by this diff that a struct/@type change would make unrepresentable beyond what's already flagged and reasoned through in (c) above -- attrs remain plain maps consistent with Letflow.Entities.Definitions' own established convention, not a regression. No docs/issues/ filing warranted from this review.

Verdict: PASS. No BLOCKER or actionable rework items. Routing to ORCH; TEST-DESIGNER may proceed per WF-02's Step 2d gate.
